scope: Applied empirical study of low-label output calibration for static overall music valence/arousal prediction; existing calibration rules, not a new algorithm.
evidence_policy: L1 = retrieved full-text sections or first-party resource documentation; L2 = retrieved abstract; L3 = verified metadata only. Levels describe the actual retrieved evidence, not the presumed availability of a PDF. Every record specifies unsupported claims.

study_claim_boundary.source: Delegating user's task specification; no experiment logs or result tables inspected in this literature-only task.
study_claim_boundary.provided_design: Official DEAM static overall valence/arousal targets; frozen MERT-v1-95M; temporal mean pooling and MLP regression; calibration using 5 or 10 labeled target items; none, offset, identity-regularized affine, half-offset and arousal-only half-offset comparisons.
study_claim_boundary.provided_results: Limited average positive gains in DEAM development and 74 new songs; positive gains for the primary 10-label arousal-only half-offset setting in an external PMEmo subset described by the user as 334 groups.
cannot_support: The literature does not verify these project results, subset counts, grouping unit, uncertainty intervals or significance.
No literature record establishes that five or ten target labels are universally sufficient.
No originality, state-of-the-art, universal positive-transfer or clinical effectiveness guarantee is made.
The term calibration here means supervised output bias/scale correction for regression, not probabilistic confidence calibration.

records.title: Developing a benchmark for emotional analysis of music
records.evidence_location: Publisher: Annotations; Task definition 2013; Evaluation metrics. Official resource landing page.
supported_claims: DEAM includes valence/arousal annotations and distinguishes static whole-excerpt ratings from continuous temporal annotations.
The 2013 static ratings were provided separately, rather than derived from the dynamic ratings.
The benchmark paper reports CCC in addition to correlation and error metrics.
citable_sentences: DEAM provides both static overall ratings and time-varying valence/arousal annotations, with static ratings collected separately from the dynamic traces.
The distinction between static and dynamic targets is part of the original DEAM benchmark design.
cannot_support: Equating official static labels with the temporal mean of dynamic labels.
Claiming the project's 74-song evaluation is an official DEAM benchmark split.
All 1,802 items having identical static collection procedures; the paper describes changes across collection years.
records.access_limitations: Publisher full-text sections retrieved; manual PDF extraction failed. Do not infer exact CSV column names from the paper alone.

cannot_support: The project's 334 groups being the full PMEmo dataset or the official test set.
Metadata and repository summary establishing all original annotation instructions or perceived-versus-induced semantics.
Assuming 2018 and updated 2019 release preprocessing are identical.

records.title: MERT: Acoustic Music Understanding Model with Large-Scale Self-supervised Training
records.evidence_location: Paper Section 4.1 Probing Protocol; official checkpoint card Model Usage and checkpoint summary.
supported_claims: MERT is a self-supervised acoustic music representation model.
The paper's probing protocol freezes the pretrained backbone and trains a simple downstream model, typically an MLP.
Emotion-score regression is among the downstream tasks, evaluated on EmoMusic rather than the present project's DEAM split.
The official MERT-v1-95M card documents temporal mean reduction of hidden-state representations and a 95M checkpoint.
citable_sentences: MERT evaluates music representations through a probing protocol that freezes the pretrained backbone and trains a lightweight downstream predictor.
The official MERT-v1-95M documentation illustrates temporal mean pooling of hidden-state representations for clip-level use.
cannot_support: MERT already solving the present low-label DEAM-to-PMEmo calibration protocol.
Calling temporal mean pooling plus an MLP a new architecture.
Guaranteed DEAM or PMEmo superiority of the 95M checkpoint.
Quoting a pretraining-hours count without resolving the discrepancy between the paper and checkpoint card.
records.planned_use: Frozen feature-extractor and mean-pooled MLP precedent.
records.metadata_notes: arXiv first submission: 2023-05-31; arXiv explicitly states accepted by ICLR 2024. The 2024 v4 and current v5 citation_author tags list 20 authors. The repository and checkpoint BibTeX list only 18 and omit Chenghao Xiao and Zili Wang; use the version-verified 20-author list. Conference acceptance is verified through the authors' arXiv record; OpenReview content was inaccessible, so a separately inspected original conference author list is not claimed.
records.access_limitations: Relevant full-text sections retrieved as arXiv HTML; OpenReview blocked. The PDF/HTML complete document was not exhaustively audited.

records.title: A survey of music emotion recognition
records.evidence_location: Sections 2 Preliminary knowledge; 3 Feature extraction and emotion recognition; 4.1 Current challenges.
supported_claims: The survey distinguishes song-level static MER from dynamic music-emotion variation detection.
It reviews traditional and deep-learning approaches and discusses subjective emotion labels and the need for diversified datasets.
citable_sentences: Music emotion recognition includes distinct static song-level and dynamic temporal prediction settings.
Reviews of music emotion recognition identify subjective annotation and limited dataset diversity as persistent challenges.
cannot_support: A formally PRISMA-compliant systematic review; its survey title alone does not establish that methodology.
No prior calibration or linear adaptation exists.
records.planned_use: General MER landscape and static/dynamic distinction.
records.metadata_notes: Year is 2022, despite the 2021 string inside the DOI; publisher metadata records first online publication on 2022-01-22.
records.access_limitations: Publisher full-text sections retrieved through Higher Education Press; Springer page was challenged.

records.title: A Study on the Data Distribution Gap in Music Emotion Recognition
records.venue: 17th International Symposium on Computer Music Multidisciplinary Research (CMMR), acceptance stated on arXiv
records.evidence_location: Sections 3 Datasets; 4.2 The Gap: Cross-dataset Prediction; 4.3 Analyzing the Gap; 4.4 Bridging the Gap.
supported_claims: The paper investigates dimensional MER across EmoMusic, DEAM, PMEmo and two classical-music datasets.
It restricts datasets with both annotation types to static annotations and demonstrates cross-dataset distribution gaps.
Its intervention combines Jukebox embeddings with chroma features and diversified training data, rather than tiny-target output calibration.
citable_sentences: Ching and Widmer investigate static dimensional emotion recognition across multiple datasets and document a cross-dataset distribution gap.
Their approach addresses generalization through representation design and diversified training data, rather than through a small labeled-target output correction.
cannot_support: No prior cross-dataset dimensional MER study exists.
A half-offset rule or the present 5/10-label budget is established by their experiments.
Dataset scale normalization alone removes annotation or genre differences.
records.planned_use: Closest task-level motivation and explicit related-work contrast.
records.metadata_notes: arXiv submission 2025-10-06; acceptance at CMMR 2025 stated by authors. The Zenodo DOI is a repository/proceedings-related resource DOI, not silently represented as a journal DOI. Zenodo record publication is 2025-11-03, retrieved on 2026-10-08.
records.access_limitations: Core full-text sections retrieved; no result numbers copied.

records.evidence_location: Introduction; Sections 3.1 Data, 3.3 Model, 3.4 Training; Results and Discussions.
supported_claims: The study distinguishes prediction of central tendency from prediction of inter-rater variability.
It finds uncertainty in subjective ratings harder to model than their central tendency under the studied approaches.

citable_sentences: Predicting an average music-emotion rating does not by itself quantify the variability of listeners' responses.
Watcharasupat et al. distinguish mean-rating prediction from inter-rater uncertainty estimation and find the latter more difficult in their experiments.

Bootstrap uncertainty of average calibration gains being equivalent to uncertainty of individual listener responses.
This paper using MERT or validating the project's PMEmo protocol.

records.title: A Survey on Negative Transfer
records.evidence_location: Sections I Introduction; II-C Negative Transfer; IV-B Secure Transfer for Regression.
supported_claims: The survey describes negative transfer as harm to target-domain learning caused by use of source information.
It reviews approaches intended to avoid or mitigate negative transfer, including regularized regression transfer.
Its formal negative-transfer gap compares an algorithm with source information against the corresponding algorithm without it.
citable_sentences: Transfer is not guaranteed to help: source information can reduce target-domain performance, a phenomenon reviewed as negative transfer.
A conservative empirical evaluation should therefore retain an unchanged predictor as a reference when measuring the effect of adaptation.
cannot_support: Worse calibration than no correction automatically satisfying the survey's formal source-versus-target-only negative-transfer definition.
A guaranteed-safe or universally positive half-offset rule.
An identity-centered affine objective being exactly the original ridge estimator.
records.planned_use: Risk-aware related work; distinguish calibration harm from strict formal negative transfer.
records.metadata_notes: Initial preprint 2020; inspected arXiv v4 dated 2021. arXiv lists a provisional 2022 journal reference. Publisher-deposited metadata verifies final issue 10(2), February 2023, 305--329; use 2023 for final journal citation. The DOI's 2022 string is not the issue year.
records.access_limitations: Full text inspected is the 2021 preprint, not an exhaustively audited final 2023 article. Broad definitional claim corroborated by arXiv abstract.
